subject: CloudPresence SI integration: marketplace billing & private-offer asks
messages:
From: Evan Reed <evan@cloudpresence.com>

Cc: Dana Li <dana@siworks.io>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Quick sync: SI partner integration + marketplace billing model

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudPresence is ready to start a technical evaluation for a managed SI integration with Redwood. Two items we need to surface early:

1) Marketplace billing / private-offer flow: our procurement teams prefer an ISV-private-offer model (Azure/AWS style) where we invoice customers via CloudPresence and Redwood invoices us. Can Redwood support a private-offer or partner-managed billing mapping?

2) Entitlements & seats: we need a way to gate features (dedicated capacity vs hosted) via license entitlements, ideally with programmatic entitlement checks (token + account mapping).

I've attached our onboarding checklist and a high-level SOW. Could you loop in the right folks on the Redwood product/marketplace side so we can align on timeline?

Best,
Evan Reed
Head of Partnerships, CloudPresence Inc

Thanks, Tessa. Quick scan notes from product/marketplace side:

- Private offers: we currently support private-offer flows for AWS Marketplace and have an in-work path for Azure. That said, the partner-managed invoicing model (Redwood invoices partner, partner invoices customer) triggers two exceptions: 1) revenue recognition & reseller agreement updates, 2) entitlement sync for customer accounts created via partner offers.

- Entitlements: Redwood has an account metadata service and a feature-flag gating layer, but we don't have a turnkey partner-entitlement API yet. We can prototype a webhook-based sync or a token-scoped entitlement key in Q1, but it will require engineering effort.

- Dedicated capacity mapping: we can map dedicated GPU pools to partner SKUs, but we need to clarify billing cadence (monthly reserve vs usage).

Open questions for engineering:
1) Karthik: estimate for a token-scoped entitlement check + webhook consumer (proto) — rough band?
2) Karthik/Jonas: any red flags for supporting partner-managed private offers across regions?

I'll hold a 30-minute sync on Thu 12/3 at 11:00 AM PT for a quick playbook review. Calendar invite to follow.

--Marissa Cole
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Quick sync: SI partner integration + marketplace billing model

On Thu, Dec 3, 2026 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Entitlements: Redwood has an account metadata service and a feature-flag gating layer, but we don't have a turnkey partner-entitlement API yet. We can prototype a webhook-based sync or a token-scoped entitlement key in Q1, but it will require engineering effort.

Notes from engineering after the quick sync:
- Token-scoped entitlement key: low-medium effort. We can add an optional entitlement object to our token introspection endpoint and short-lived partner tokens. Estimate: 3 engineers, 4–6 weeks to ship a prototype (internal alpha) if we don't block on infra changes.
- Webhook consumer approach: easier to iterate, but it introduces more operational burden (retries, mapping edge cases). Good for POC.
- Marketplace private offers: the bigger complexity is customer identity reconciliation (marketplace account IDs vs Redwood org ids). We'll need a reconciliation table and a simple admin UI to map partner offers to Redwood orgs. Estimate additional 2 sprints for reconciliation UI + mapping APIs.

Technical blockers: KMS key separation (partners requested separate key control for some customers) — we currently only support Redwood-managed KMS for hosted model keys. Private KMS/HSM for partner-managed keys is non-trivial and will be scoped as a separate project.

I'll draft a short RFC and cost/effort estimate and post to INT-872.

—Karthik
Senior Engineer, Integrations
Redwood Inference

Folks — commercial notes from procurement POV:

- If CloudPresence wants partner-managed billing, we will need a reseller addendum on top of our standard MSA covering: payment terms, tax handling, refund flow, and SLA pass-through. Legal will want to review.
- Pricing model: recommend we offer two SKU bands for partners: "partner-managed reserved CPU/GPU" (monthly reserve) and "partner-managed on-demand" (metered usage). Make sure the SKU IDs are stable for private-offer linking.
- Credits/discounts: CloudPresence asked for a launch credit for the first 90 days. We can approve a small promotional credit contingent on a 12-month minimum commitment (delegate to Sales Ops).

I'll capture proposed SKU IDs in the deal record (CP-2026-1047) and circulate a short commercial appendix for legal.

—Priyom Das
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
